conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of the hospitalists. I understand you've been having a hoarse voice for a few days?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started about three days ago. It’s been getting worse, and now I can barely speak above a whisper.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any trouble breathing, stridor, or chest tightness?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I’m not having trouble breathing. Just the hoarseness. I did feel a little sick to my stomach that morning with loose stools, but that’s gone now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I also see you were recently seen by your laryngologist for vocal cord issues. Can you tell me about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, Dr. Patel diagnosed me with paradoxical vocal fold motion disorder. I have scarring and swelling on one of my vocal cords. He wanted me to have a bronchoscopy soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s right. And you had an appointment scheduled for today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, at 1 PM. But my voice got so bad last night, I came to the ER instead.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understandable. We did a neck X-ray, and there’s no sign of airway blockage or swelling. Your oxygen levels are good, and you’re not in distress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Could the cleaning products my daughter used have made it worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. Chemical irritants can aggravate vocal cord inflammation, especially with your existing condition. Smoking can also make it worse—have you been smoking?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I should stop… but yes, I still smoke occasionally.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. It’s tough, but quitting would really help your vocal cords and overall health. For now, we’ll continue your omeprazole for reflux, which can also irritate the voice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also gave you albuterol and ipratropium in the ER, which helped a bit. We’ll keep that available if you need it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. What about my other medications? My blood pressure has been a little high lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your blood pressure is around 142/84, which is better than last admission. We’re increasing your enalapril from 5 to 10 mg daily to help control it, especially since you have hyperaldosteronism.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my diabetes and headaches? I haven’t had a migraine lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood sugar is stable, so we’re continuing glyburide. No headaches today, which is good. We’re keeping your topiramate and propranolol for prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One lab note: you have a mild metabolic acidosis, likely from your acetazolamide for pseudotumor cerebri. We’ll continue it for now, but your neurologist may adjust it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. So am I going to be here long?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Actually, your laryngologist was consulted, and he thinks you’re stable to go home. You’re scheduled to see him today at 1 PM for your bronchoscopy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, I didn’t know they’d reschedule it for today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll evaluate for any fixed airway narrowing. In the meantime, we’re sending you home with an inhaler and updated meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are stable, and you’re still breathing well. We’re clearing you for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What changes should I watch for?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or come back if you develop breathing trouble, fever, chest pain, or if you can’t keep fluids down. Otherwise, keep your appointment with Dr. Patel.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my medications—anything changed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Enalapril is now 10 mg daily. Glyburide is increased to 5 mg. Everything else stays the same. And please consider the smoking cessation program—we can help you get started.
